title: Discrete Mathematics
objectives:
Combinatorial reasoning underlies all analysis of a computer system and a discrete mathematics
course seeks to develop proficiency in basic discrete math problem-solving in the way that a
calculus course develops proficiency in basic analysis problem-solving. This course should teach
students to think logically and mathematically, reason and model combinatorially, and use discrete
structures. Some important themes interwoven in this course are mathematical reasoning and
mathematical induction, combinatorial analysis and enumeration, discrete structures, graphs, and
modeling the problems using them.
syllabus:
- Induction and Recursion
Mathematical Reasoning, Mathematical Induction, Strong Induction and Well-Ordering,
Recursive Definitions and Structural Induction, Recursive Algorithms
- Logics and Proofs
Propositional Logic, Propositional Equivalences, Predicates and Quantifiers, Nested Quantifiers,
Rules of Inference, Introduction to Proofs, Proof Methods, and Strategy
- Counting
The Basics of Counting, The Product Rule, The Sum Rule, the Tree Diagram, The Pigeonhole
Principle, Permutations and Combinations, Binomial Coefficients, Binomial Theorem, Pascal’s
Identities and Triange, Vander monde's Identity, Generalized Permutations and Combinations,
Permutations with Repetitions, Combinations with Repetitions, Distributing Objects into Boxes,
Algorithms For Generating Permutations and Combinations
- Advanced Counting Techniques
Recurrence Relations, Modeling with Recurrence Relations, Fibonacci Numbers, The Tower of
Hanoi, Catalan Numbers, Solving Linear Recurrence Relations, Linear Homogeneous Recurrence
Relations with Constant Coefficients, Linear Nonhomogeneous Recurrence Relations with
Constant Coefficients, Divide-and-Conquer Algorithms, and Recurrence Relations, Formal Power
Series, Generating Functions, Counting Problems and Generating Functions, Inclusion-Exclusion,
Applications of Inclusion-Exclusion
- Relations
Relations and Their Properties, n-ary Relations and Their Applications, Representing Relations,
Closures of Relations, Equivalence Relations, Partial Orderings.
- Graphs
Graphs and Graph Models, Incidence and Adjacency Matrices of a Graph, Graph Terminology
and Special Types of Graphs, Complete graphs, Bipartite Graphs, Representing Graphs and Graph
Isomorphism, Connectivity, Euler and Hamilton Paths and Circuits, Algorithm to Construct Euler

Circuits, Ore’s Theorem, Dirac’s Theorem, Shortest-Path Problems, Dijkstra’s Algorithm, Planar
Graphs, Euler’s Formula, Kuratowski’s Theorem, Graph Coloring
- Trees
Introduction to Trees, Rooted Trees, m-ary Trees, Applications of Trees, Huffman Coding, Tree
Traversal, Traversal Algorithms: Preorder, Inorder, Postorder, Spanning Trees, Depth First Search
and Breadth First Search Algorithms, Minimum Spanning Trees, Prim’s Algorithm, Kruskal’s
Algorithm
textbooks:
1. R. P. Grimaldi, Discrete and Combinatorial Mathematics: An Applied Introduction, 5th Edition,
Pearson, 2017.
2. K. H. Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, 7th Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2011.
3. S. S. Epp, Discrete Mathematics with Applications, 4th Edition, Brooks Cole, 2010.
